Primary, foreign and composite keys

Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the entities and relationships chapter, relationships-workbook.md, relationships-answers.md, equipment-model.svg and the four model CSVs (Borrower, Category, Equipment, Loan). Use fictional data and a disposable copy or paper. No SQL setup or student account is required. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Primary, foreign and composite keys

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Choose keys that preserve valid borrowing history. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

2. Matching descriptions

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

EquipmentID identifies each item. The chosen primary key must be unique and required. Descriptions and borrower display labels can repeat. A primary key may use one field or a group of fields. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

3. Keys and their jobs

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example with teacher explanation

Minimal means no attribute can be removed without losing uniqueness under the agreed rules. Minimal does not mean shortest text. A composite key can be a primary key. A foreign key may refer to another table or the same table and its values may repeat. Our required foreign keys refer to existing parent primary keys. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html . Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

4. A loan uses three identifiers

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher modelling

Trace L003 to Borrower B001 (Learner A), Equipment E03 (Recorder), then Equipment.CategoryID C03 to Category C03 (Audio). Equipment.CategoryID is another required FK. The foreign keys identify the referenced borrower and item, not this loan event. BorrowerID repeats in Loan because borrowers can have multiple events. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

5. A pair that can repeat

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

These are the two existing events in the dataset. L005 is returned, L002 is active. Do not use the borrower/item pair alone as Loan’s key. Adding a new future event needs a new LoanID and separate checks against overlapping active loans. An FK alone does not enforce that business rule. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

6. Keys that reject the right errors

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 2, 3, 6, 7 and 9 as selected practice. Duplicate L001 violates PK uniqueness. B999 is absent from Borrower, so a required FK must reject it. For the separate WorkshopEnrolment example, assume one enrolment per borrower/workshop pair: (BorrowerID, WorkshopID) can be a composite PK. Either field alone may repeat. Example pairs B001/W01, B001/W02 and B002/W01 are permitted, while another B001/W01 is not. The extension is not a fifth table in the equipment model. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

7. A repeated foreign key

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

No. BorrowerID is a foreign key in Loan and may repeat. LoanID is the chosen primary key of Loan and must remain unique. B001 must exist in Borrower for both references. A field can have different key roles in different tables. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

8. Rules beyond the sample

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

Candidate-key status depends on the intended rules for all valid data, including future records. The school may register two borrowers with the same label. A sample can expose a failed uniqueness claim but cannot establish a permanent uniqueness requirement by itself. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.
